title: Account takeover and the laundering that follows
definition: The acquisition of control of a victim's account — by credential theft, by impersonation, or by the coercion of the account holder — followed by the use of that account to move value, either into an account the attacker controls or on to third parties. The defining feature is a change in who controls the account, which the transaction history alone does not show.
evidence_to_cite: the session, device and authentication logs
the transfer records made after the change of control
the evidence of the change of control, cited by its own source id
benign_explanations: A customer who travelled and began a session from a new device in a new country.
A customer who replaced a phone and was signing in for the first time.
A customer whose password expired and who reset it before a scheduled payment.
A joint account holder returning to online banking after a long absence.

sources.citation: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, guidance on account takeover, and the money laundering offences that may follow it, summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.
